sentences.text: Nasu-Hakola disease, whose full name is polycystic lipomembranous osteodysplasia with sclerosing leukoencephaly, is recorded as caused by the genes TREM2 and TYROBP in a curated database [e_ce47505eb383] [e_508743311498].
Alzheimer disease 17 is also tied to TREM2, according to OMIM [e_2b7cacb8c6f0].
Constellate computed that the two conditions share TREM2 as a causal gene, at confidence 0.9 [e_07c8f34728ca].
That shared-gene link is inferred, meaning it was calculated from the two curated links [e_07c8f34728ca].
TREM2 and TYROBP are both recorded as taking part in two immune-related pathways, one named DAP12 interactions [e_559f3096d1b6] [e_598144ced4a5] [e_a59a37d44b28] [e_f5695f800be5].
Nasu-Hakola disease has two curated features, frontal lobe dementia and bone cysts, both listed as very frequent [e_058c15a5b786] [e_1d4f94f48353].
These edges do not show that the two conditions are the same illness or that they act alike, and they list no studies or treatments [e_07c8f34728ca].
